# Melrakki Systems

> Melrakki Systems is a UK engineering company, based in Kent, that designs autonomous off-grid power for critical equipment operating beyond reliable infrastructure: surveillance, communications, sensors and autonomous systems such as drones. It offers two standard platforms (Harka Solar and Harka Hybrid), bespoke off-grid power engineering, and Greni, an off-grid drone charging and docking station that is a working prototype in field test and not yet for sale.

Melrakki designs the power beneath the equipment, not the equipment itself. Every system is "engineered from the load backwards". The method starts with the mission, the load and its duty cycle, then the location and conditions, and only then the generation, storage, backup and platform. Systems are sized for "the worst credible week" the site will see, not the average day. Melrakki treats resilience as reducing dependencies (grid, fuel, site visits) rather than adding a bigger backup. These are Melrakki's own design principles, not external standards.

Melrakki is a new company name. Its experience comes from its founder and team's earlier work: 13 years building off-grid solar surveillance and power, including co-design of solar CCTV infrastructure across 58 sites in Kazakhstan, plus deployments in oil and gas, highways, construction and critical infrastructure. It does not publish customer names, case studies, certifications or defence approvals.

Published platform figures are at a 100 W continuous load. Where pages differ, the specification table on the Harka page is authoritative for Harka figures, and the Greni page is authoritative for Greni's status. Last reviewed: 2026-09-28.

## Platforms and services

- [Harka platforms](https://www.melrakki.systems/harka/): Two standard autonomous off-grid power platforms on a 6 m manual mast with a 1,080 W solar array (3 × 360 W) at 24 VDC. **Harka Solar (MK-HK-S6)**: 400 Ah AGM battery, 75 h battery reserve at 100 W, no fuel or engine. **Harka Hybrid (MK-HK-H6)**: 220 Ah AGM battery, 41 h battery reserve at 100 W, and a Stage V generator on HVO renewable diesel that starts at 40% state of charge to recharge the battery. It runs up to 1,840 h at 100 W from a 125 L tank before refuelling. Both are commercial. Remote monitoring is optional. Not certified for hazardous areas.
- [Harka Solar brochure (PDF)](https://www.melrakki.systems/Melrakki-Harka-Solar.pdf): Full technical data for MK-HK-S6, including dimensions, weight, battery type and cycle life, and transport.
- [Harka Hybrid brochure (PDF)](https://www.melrakki.systems/Melrakki-Harka-Hybrid.pdf): Full technical data for MK-HK-H6, including generator engine and alternator, dimensions and weight.
- [Greni](https://www.melrakki.systems/greni/): Off-grid charging and docking station for autonomous drones (MK-GR-01): skid-mounted solar hybrid power, tilting solar array, lithium storage. Status: working prototype in field test with a leading UK organisation, results confidential. No performance figures, compatibilities or approvals are published. Early interest can be registered.
- [Bespoke engineering](https://www.melrakki.systems/bespoke/): Off-grid power engineered around a customer's device, site and constraints when no standard platform fits: unusual loads or voltages, harsher environments, or limits on size, weight, signature or mounting. Includes a requirement brief builder.

## How Melrakki designs power

- [Off-grid power systems for remote sites](https://www.melrakki.systems/off-grid-power/): The main guide. Architectures compared by what they depend on; autonomy versus endurance; what solar alone can carry in a UK winter (about 25 W average in a southern UK December from a 1,080 W array); designing for sites that are hard to reach; battery lifecycle.
- [Designing power from the load backwards](https://www.melrakki.systems/resilience/designing-power-from-the-load-backwards/): The sizing method step by step, and the nine numbers to bring to a first conversation.
- [About Melrakki](https://www.melrakki.systems/about/): The company, its six design principles, and its founder, Simon Legrand (co-founder of Sunstone Systems, 2011), with his documented experience.

## Applications and sectors

- [Solar-powered surveillance](https://www.melrakki.systems/solar-powered-surveillance/): Power for remote CCTV: device load behaviour, a load worksheet, winter sizing, and when solar-only or hybrid is the honest answer.
- [Remote communications power](https://www.melrakki.systems/telecommunications/): Power for radio, telemetry and network nodes; backup versus autonomy; what a small platform can carry (macro mobile base stations are beyond it). Melrakki supplies power, not radios.
- [Drone dock power](https://www.melrakki.systems/drone-dock-power/): Why a drone dock is a harder load than a camera (continuous baseline plus charge peaks). Melrakki powers only dock and aircraft combinations it has tested and passed.
- [Critical infrastructure](https://www.melrakki.systems/critical-infrastructure/): Remote assets whose security or monitoring shares a power supply with the asset it protects, and where independent power belongs.
- [Oil and gas](https://www.melrakki.systems/oil-and-gas/): Surveillance and monitoring power for remote oil and gas sites; platforms are sited outside hazardous zones; climate and fuel considerations.
- [Defence and security](https://www.melrakki.systems/defence-and-security/): Signature (acoustic, thermal, exhaust, resupply) and logistics as design inputs for perimeter, border and compound power. No defence approvals or contracts are claimed.

## Field notes

Field notes are written by the founder. They explain and argue; they are not product specifications. Where a note describes a product, the product page takes precedence.

- [When the grid goes away](https://www.melrakki.systems/resilience/when-the-grid-goes-away/): The main field note. Resilience as fewer dependencies rather than a bigger backup; redundancy versus independence; power as infrastructure for other infrastructure; the worst credible week.
- [The last mile of resilience](https://www.melrakki.systems/resilience/the-last-mile-of-resilience/): Why critical infrastructure is only as resilient as its furthest node. Includes Melrakki's working definition of autonomous edge infrastructure, offered as a way of thinking rather than an established industry category.
- [When the infrastructure becomes the vulnerability](https://www.melrakki.systems/resilience/when-the-infrastructure-becomes-the-vulnerability/): Why a robust security system can be operationally fragile, and moving the dependency boundary closer to the asset.
- [The sabotage problem](https://www.melrakki.systems/resilience/the-sabotage-problem/): Sabotage as a dependency problem as well as a security problem. Separates what authoritative sources document from what they do not predict.
- [When the drone has its own power station](https://www.melrakki.systems/resilience/off-grid-drone-infrastructure/): Why persistent remote drone operation is an energy and infrastructure problem, UK BVLOS context, and where Greni (prototype) fits.
- [The true cost of a diesel generator on a remote site](https://www.melrakki.systems/resilience/the-true-cost-of-a-diesel-generator/): Why the real cost of remote diesel is logistics, site visits, signature and downtime, and when diesel is still the right answer.
